primitives.name: Multivariate GLMM Team Strength
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Multivariate GLMM: each team j has (b_j^o offensive, b_j^d defensive, b_j^w win-propensity) ~ N_3(0, G*) with unstructured 3×3 covariance (block-diagonal G over p teams).

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of the paper lies in modeling team performance through a multivariate normal distribution of latent variables—offense, defense, and win propensity—captured via correlated random effects. This allows for joint inference that improves prediction over univariate models. The mathematical framework uses a joint likelihood function integrating over team-level random effects, enabling simultaneous modeling of binary outcomes (win/loss) and continuous game-level metrics (yards, sacks, etc.). The assumption of conditional independence given these random effects simplifies computation while preserving hierarchical structure. The model's strength lies in its ability to infer latent correlations between efficiency and outcome, such as how offensive strength correlates with win probability. However, it assumes multivariate normality of random effects and conditional independence, which may fail under sparse data or extreme outliers. The extension to NFL data via modern variational inference or Laplace approximations allows practical deployment in GSE.
